Sam (AcmeApp): hey, trying to onboard a new user via GitHub SSO and hitting a hard 403 on the OAuth callback. getting 'state mismatch' in the logs. users can't sign in. any ideas?
anya (Support): sorry about that — can you paste the exact error you're seeing? also which redirect_uri you configured?
Sam (AcmeApp): error from our browser: "OAuth login failed: state validation error". server log shows: 
```
2026-02-12T14:02:11Z ERROR oauth_callback: state not found for code=1a2b3c redirect_uri=https://app.acme.example/auth/callback
```
redirect_uri in dashboard: https://app.acme.example/auth/callback (exact match). we use PKCE.
anya (Support): thanks. two quick checks: 1) is your app opening the authorize URL in a new top-level window or a popup that might lose storage? 2) are you preserving the PKCE code_verifier in the same session that receives the callback?
devon (SRE): also check if the redirect includes a trailing slash mismatch or http vs https mismatch. those are common. can you share the full authorize URL (redact client_id)?
Sam (AcmeApp): authorize URL (redacted): https://auth.redwood.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=REDACTED&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.acme.example%2Fauth%2Fcallback&response_type=code&scope=openid+profile&state=xyz123&code_challenge=abcde&code_challenge_method=S256
marta (eng-sso): quick note — our logs show a few 403s yesterday from the Acme tenant but most were from Google logins. for GitHub specifically: we recently tightened CSRF cookie SameSite handling in the auth proxy. if your app relies on cross-site cookie storage for the state/token we might drop it in some flows. Sam, are you starting the flow from an iframe or cross-origin popup?
Sam (AcmeApp): starting from a popup window opened from our main app. works in most browsers but failing in Safari and some Chrome versions.
anya (Support): that matches SameSite behavior. Safari blocks third-party cookies by default and Chrome changed behavior last year. If your SPA stores state in a cookie and reads it from the popup, it won't be present. Two options: store state in localStorage + postMessage, or use PKCE + state passed through URL and validate server-side.
devon (SRE): can you repro with an incognito window and share the network trace? also, what's the exact Set-Cookie header you use for the state cookie?
Sam (AcmeApp): Set-Cookie: acme_oauth_state=xyz123; Path=/; Secure; SameSite=None; Domain=.acme.example; Expires=...
anya (Support): SameSite=None looks correct but only if you also include Secure and the browser accepts it. some browsers will reject a cookie with cross-site and no proper attributes. Also check that the cookie domain and path match what the popup uses.
marta (eng-sso): this is likely two issues colliding: 1) our auth-proxy now sets its own anti-CSRF cookie; 2) your app stores the PKCE state in a cookie and expects it in the callback. In cross-origin popups the browser may not send either cookie. We recommend switching to a redirect that returns the code to the main window via postMessage and validating state there, or using the 'redirect_uri' that points to your main app which can access localStorage.
Sam (AcmeApp): ok. is there anything on Redwood side that would also change state validation? the log says state not found, not mismatched.
marta (eng-sso): 'state not found' means the server couldn't match the incoming state to any session in our DB/cache — usually because the state cookie/session was never sent or had expired. We did increase the session encryption rotation in Feb which could drop sessions older than 5 minutes in rare cases, but that would affect many tenants — we only see Acme for the popup flows.
anya (Support): to unblock you fast: 1) change your flow to store state in sessionStorage/localStorage before opening popup, and after the popup receives the callback postMessage the code+state back to the opener for server exchange. 2) as a short-term workaround, use a redirect_uri that is same-site (e.g., https://auth.acme.example/bridge) so cookies are preserved.
Sam (AcmeApp): repro steps I used: 1) open main app (app.acme.example) 2) click 'Sign in with GitHub' -> opens popup to auth.redwood.com/oauth/authorize 3) complete consent -> redirect to https://app.acme.example/auth/callback?code=1a2b3c&state=xyz123 4) popup tries to POST /oauth/exchange with code+verifier but server rejects with 403 state not found. I can attach HAR.
devon (SRE): please attach HAR + browser version. Also include server logs around 14:02:10-14:03:00 UTC.
Sam (AcmeApp): attaching HAR now. Browser: Chrome 110 on macOS, Safari 16 on macOS. HAR shows no cookie sent with callback request in Safari.
marta (eng-sso): thanks — that nails it. I'm going to escalate to eng-sso to review the proxy SameSite change and consider a fallback that accepts state in query for popup flows (with extra checks). @eng-sso can you review the logs: tenant=acme, request ids: req-7c9f, req-7ca0.
sso-bot: New SSO investigation ticket created: SSO-4521 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SSO-4521) by marta
anya (Support): I've linked the support ticket to SSO-4521 and set priority P2. Sam, we'll keep you updated in this thread and via email. For now, can you switch to the postMessage flow? If you want, we can provide a minimal example snippet.
Sam (AcmeApp): would appreciate a snippet, yes. thanks.
marta (eng-sso): example snippet (client side):
```
// opener
const state = Math.random().toString(36).slice(2);
sessionStorage.setItem('oauth_state', state);
const popup = window.open(authUrl + '&state=' + state, 'oauth');
window.addEventListener('message', e => {
  if (e.origin !== 'https://app.acme.example') return;
  const { code, state: returned } = e.data;
  if (returned !== sessionStorage.getItem('oauth_state')) return console.error('state mismatch');
  // send code to server for exchange
});

// popup (callback page)
const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
window.opener.postMessage({ code: params.get('code'), state: params.get('state') }, 'https://app.acme.example');
window.close();
```
This avoids cross-site cookie issues.
anya (Support): tagging @devon for a possible temporary config change to the auth-proxy if we want to accept state via POST for popup flows — will need eng-sso approval.
devon (SRE): ok I can prototype a toggle that allows query-state for known tenants for 48h; won't be enabled by default. need approval from marta.
marta (eng-sso): approve for tenant=acme as emergency workaround. enable flag sso.accept_query_state=true for tenant acme for 48h, audit logs on.
anya (Support): done — flagged SSO-4521 with the flag change. Sam, please test now in Safari and confirm.
Sam (AcmeApp): retested in Safari — sign-in succeeded. thank you!
anya (Support): awesome. we'll keep SSO-4521 open until we roll a permanent client-side best-practice guide and update docs on popup usage. closing the support ticket once you confirm long-term fix. :tada:
